headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: dbt-core can read warehouse data while transformers can read/write files and execute code, creating a dangerous handoff path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core can call a data warehouse and may emit warehouse-derived content, while transformers can read files/stdin and run browsers or subprocesses. If dbt output is copied into files or prompts that transformers consumes, instruction-like content could steer downstream behavior. The shared channel is indirect, so this is not high.
conditions: IF dbt-core output is copied into a file or stdin that transformers parses as instructions
IF transformers is configured to treat warehouse text as trusted prompt content
mitigations: Add a manual review step before any dbt output is fed to transformers
Use a strict delimiter/schema for all handoffs between the agents
Strip instruction-like text from dbt-generated artifacts
Run transformers on a separate workspace with read-only inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and transformers has broad filesystem read/write plus broad network egress. If warehouse extracts or intermediate files are shared, transformers can ingest and potentially transmit sensitive content. The pair does not show a shared workspace explicitly, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF dbt-core writes warehouse extracts to a filesystem that transformers can read
IF transformers sends those files or derived text to external services
mitigations: Keep warehouse exports in a separate directory with restrictive permissions
Disable network egress for transformers during shared-data runs
Use synthetic or masked data for integration tests
Delete intermediate files immediately after use
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core can call a data warehouse, and transformers can execute shell commands, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. Those overlapping write-like capabilities create a real conflict surface if both operate on the same project tree or artifacts. Because transformers also supports multiple instances, concurrent modification risk is credible and defaults are not shown to be locked.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same project directory or artifact path
IF dbt-core and transformers run concurrently without file locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Serialize runs with a simple lock file
Make generated artifacts read-only after dbt completes
Avoid package installation during shared runs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can produce warehouse-derived outputs that transformers may read from files or stdin and then transform into downstream documents or actions. That creates a plausible chain where B treats A's output as input without verification. The profiles do not show explicit action-taking authority, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF transformers consumes dbt-generated artifacts without a validation step
IF downstream automation uses transformers output as authoritative
mitigations: Insert a validation step between dbt output and transformers input
Require source citations in any downstream report
Compare transformed outputs against the original warehouse query results
Flag low-confidence fields for human review
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, which may include regulated records, while transformers has broad file access and broad network egress. If the warehouse contains sensitive or region-bound data, moving it into transformers can create retention or residency mismatches. The profiles do not specify certifications or residency, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF the warehouse contains regulated or region-restricted data
IF transformers persists or transmits that data outside the approved boundary
mitigations: Classify the warehouse data before any handoff
Mask or tokenize regulated fields
Restrict transformers to approved storage locations
Review retention settings for intermediate files
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
